independent_checks.result: From e^(hx)*phi(x)/e^(h^2/2)=phi(x-h), the correct tilted mean is h. Integrating the tilt gives L(t+h)/L(h); the printed denominator L(t) fails at t=0,h=1, yielding e^(1/2) for a Gaussian.

Differentiating log L gives (L*L''-L'^2)/L^2. For L(h)=e^(h^2/2), h=1, printed expression equals 2e^(-1/2)-1, while the tilted variance equals1. The omitted factor is visible on the page; K'' is the correct intended identity.

independent_checks.location: p3 periodic Laplace and p13 Fourier comparison
independent_checks.result: Laplace transform of standard Gaussian has positive quadratic exponent; its characteristic function has negative exponent. A positive Fourier exponent gives nonintegrable absolute difference and cannot be the stated local comparison.

Psi(0)=1, so printed L=1-c*Psi has L(0)=1-c. The p19 definition and actual Gaussian-cosine integral give L=e^(t^2/2)*Psi. The explicit q bound uses c*B=1/2, ensuring a nonnegative normalized density; P''(0)=0 preserves unit variance.

Its c1,c2>0, c1^2+c2^2=1 assumptions allow c1=sqrt(3)/2,c2=1/2. Integrating the printed double convolution yields mass c1/c2=sqrt(3). Replacing the second scale c1 by c2 restores mass1 and Gaussian variance1.
